Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Arun Monga
Petitioner is before this Court seeking grant of bail in relation to FIR No. 815/2022 dated 29.07.2022, under Sections 498A/306/34 of the IPC registered at Police Station Subhash Palace.
2. The case set up by the prosecution based on statement of complainant, as per FIR, is that the complainant's younger sister, i.e. victim (deceased), got married to the applicant.

One child i.e. son,
Jayant is also born from the wedlock.

It is alleged that for more than eight years since the marriage,
the applicant and his family members, namely Usha Nayyar (mother), Nisha and Sunita (sisters),
Kastoori Lal (father), and Prem Gopal (uncle), subjected complainant's sister to torture, physical assault and cruelty in relation to

2.1 The applicant used to demand money from the complainant's family, asserting that since the marriage was a court marriage, whatever money was saved for the wedding should be given to him,
and he would threaten to divorce complainant's sister if the money was not paid.
On three occasions, the complainant gave the applicant Rs. 6 lakhs, but despite which the Applicant used to beat his sister.
2.2 It is further alleged that two to three months prior, the applicant beat the prosecutrix severely and even called his neighbours on mobile to say that he had beaten her black and blue.

When the complainant's mother visited the applicant's house to enquire, the applicant abused her, demanded Amandeep vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4327890/
1 Rs. 7 lakhs, and threatened to kill the prosecutrix if the money was not paid.

sentences.text: When the complainant tried to reason with the Applicant over the phone, being in Sikkim at that time, he was also threatened.
Applicant and his family continued to demand Rs. 7 lakhs.
2.3 On 11.07.2022, when the complainant returned to Delhi, Applicant sent him an audio message on WhatsApp, asking why he had not met him and threatening to come himself.
That night, Nisha also called the complainant's mother, threatening that deceased victim would not be spared if Rs. 7 lakhs was not paid.
On 12.07.2022, at about 9:00 PM, Applicant came with the victim to the complainant's house armed with a sharp sword, with the intention to kill her, and attacked other family members.
His mother saved herself by closing the door, while Applicant struck at the door with the sword.
On seeing this, neighbour Jitendra dialled 112, and police caught hold of Applicant with the sword and kept him at the police station for four hours.
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/09/2025 at 23:10:07 2.4 Since Applicant had left his son alone at his house, 24 km away, and Jayant had called the complainant through a milkman's phone, a compromise was entered into at the police station on the insistence of victim, and Applicant was excused upon his apology.
Around midnight, a settlement was recorded, and the complainant advised Applicant to avoid matrimonial discord.

2.5 It is further stated that at about 2:30 AM on 13.07.2022, after reaching home, Applicant called neighbour Rajni and threatened that he would divorce the victim within three days, would not spare the complainant, and would kill him.
Earlier also, he had threatened to kill the victim if the complainant did not meet him.
On 13.07.2022, when neighbours could not contact victim in the morning, Applicant himself called Rajni and informed that victim had died.
Thereafter, Rajni informed the complainant's wife Ranjit Kaur, who video-called Applicant, during which Applicant stated that he had killed victim and that nothing could be done against him.
2.6 The complainant reported the matter to the concerned Police Station, seeking registration of an FIR against Applicant and his family members.
However, even after two weeks, no FIR was registered, and hence, the present request was made to the SHO for necessary legal action.
3. In the aforesaid backdrop, I have heard the rival contentions.

4. Learned senior counsel for the petitioner argues on the same lines as grounds taken in the petition, i.e.:-
4.1 That the applicant has been falsely implicated.
The learned senior counsel submits that the complainant has made false allegations of dowry demand but failed to produce any supporting material.
On the contrary, the applicant advanced lakhs of rupees as loan to the complainant, which fact This is a digitally signed order.

4.2 That the prosecution seeks to implicate the applicant solely on the basis of telephonic discussions, without FSL authentication.
Such evidence, without corroborating material or allegation of an overt act, cannot sustain a charge of abetment to suicide.

Moreover, the learned counsel further submits that the liberty of the applicant cannot be curtailed merely because a transcript, which is prima facie unreliable and awaits FSL confirmation, has been placed on record.
4.3 That the allegation that the applicant instigated suicide is unsubstantiated.
No suicide note was recovered, and no injury marks were found on the deceased as per the postmortem report.
4.4 That the Applicant/Accused submits that the chargesheet was filed in August 2023, and even though the trial is already underway, only PW-1 has been partly examined, despite repeated adjournments.
There are 22 witnesses that are yet to be examined and cross-examined.
It is further submitted that the trial is likely to take considerable time and the applicant cannot be kept behind bars indefinitely.
The counsel further points out that as most witnesses are official in nature, there is no apprehension of tampering or intimidation.
4.5 That the applicant/accused has been in judicial custody since 28.06.2023 and has already undergone approximately 2 years 2 months of incarceration with unimpeachable conduct.
Moreover, nothing remains to be recovered from the Applicant.

4.6 That all other co-accused have been granted Anticipatory bail by the Ld. ASJ , Rohini Court, vide order dated 27.08.2022.
4.7
That there is no likelihood of the applicant tampering with evidence This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/09/2025 at 23:10:07 or threatening witnesses as investigation is complete, charge sheet has been filed and nothing remains to be recovered from the applicant and the case is already at the stage of prosecution evidence.
4.8 Moreover, the learned counsel further submits that the applicant/accused voluntarily surrendered without resistance, which clearly establishes that he has not attempted to abscond.
4.9 That the applicant has deep roots in society, and is the sole bread winner, and the primary care giver for his aged parents and an 8-year-old child who has a medical history of cardio.

5. Learned APP opposes the bail stating that three witnesses are still unexamined and the role attributed to the petitioner is of serious nature and in case he is let out on bail, he may try to Amandeep vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4327890/
3 influence and/or intimidate the witnesses.

sentences.text: Moreover, charges against applicant are very serious.
6. Having heard, I am of the view that it is a fit case for bail.
Let us see how.

7. It transpires that the same arguments perhaps led this Court to give an interim concession to the Applicant only to observe his conduct, as to whether he deserves the regular bail or not as is borne out from the order dated 09.07.2025.
I am in agreement with the observation made in the said order passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, then seized of the matter, being relevant, the same is reproduced herein:
"1. This hearing has been done through hybrid mode.

2. The present application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. seeks regular bail in case FIR No. 815/2022, under Sections 498A/306/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S.
Subhash Place.

3. During the pendency of the present bail application, it was brought to the attention of this Court that examination-in-chief of the 3 main witnesses, i.e., PW-1/Gurpreet Singh (brother of This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/09/2025 at 23:10:07 the deceased), PW-6/Ranjeet Kaur (sister-in-law of the deceased) and PW-7/Jitender Singh has been deferred on account of certain FSL reports.
4. Vide order dated 18.02.2025, this Court had directed the concerned DCP to take necessary steps and file the report with regard to filing of the FSL report before the learned Trial Court.
On 22.04.2025, this Court was informed that one of the FSL reports with respect to the DNA profile of the deceased has been obtained and the other FSL report would be ready by 30.04.2025.
Thereafter, it has been brought to the notice that other FSL report have still not been received.

5. Learned APP for the State submits that priority letter was sent to the FSL, however,
there is no response from the FSL as to when the said reports shall be obtained.

It is further submitted that the allegations in the chargesheet is that the applicant had attacked the brother of the deceased, i.e., PW- 1/Gurpreet Singh with a sword and CCTV footage with respect to the same is awaited from the FSL.

It is submitted that the said witness is still under examination and the apprehension of the prosecution is that the present applicant may threaten the said witness.
6. Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that the applicant has been in custody since 28.06.2023 and out of 24 witnesses, only 4 have been examined and 3 witnesses are under examinationin- chief and the remaining Amandeep vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4327890/
4 witnesses also remain to be examined.

sentences.text: It is further pointed out that necessary conditions may be imposed on the applicant in order to ensure that the evidence of the aforesaid 3 witnesses who are under examination-in-chief can be conducted.
7. In the aforesaid circumstances, it is clear that there is no clear date as to when the FSL report will be received by the prosecution which is to be placed before the learned Trial Court.

In these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the applicant may be released on interim bail during the pendency of the present bail application with certain conditions to ensure that the witnesses under examination are not influenced This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

8. In these circumstances, the applicant is directed to be released on interim bail during the pendency of the present bail application, on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties of like amount, subject to the satisfaction of learned Trial Court/Link Court, further subject to the following conditions:
i.
The applicant shall not leave the NCT of Delhi without prior permission of this Court.

ii. The applicant shall report at the concerned Police Station, once in a week,
i.e., on every Friday at 04:00 P.M. and the concerned officer is directed to release him by 04:30 P.M. after recording his presence and completion of all the necessary formalities.
iii. The applicant shall intimate the learned Trial Court by way of an affidavit and to the Investigating Officer regarding any change in residential address.
iv. The applicant shall appear before the learned Trial Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.
v. The applicant is directed to give his mobile number to the Investigating Officer and keep it operational at all times.
vi. The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, tamper with evidence or try to influence the witness in any manner.
vii. The applicant shall not in any manner contact the complainant or the relatives of the deceased.
In case, the said condition is violated the prosecution/complainant are at liberty to move appropriate application for cancellation of interim bail.

9. It is pointed out that the matter is now fixed before the learned Trial Court on 05.08.2025.
10.
Accordingly, list on 03.09.2025.

On resumed hearing today, on a query put to learned APP in case there is any reported misconduct at any time on the part of the petitioner, and/or otherwise he has tried to either directly or indirectly influence the any of the unexamined witnesses, she would submit, under instructions of the Investigating Officer, that there is nothing adverse on the record.
9. The applicant has cooperated fully during the course of investigation, including appearing before investigating authorities whenever required.
There has been no attempt by the applicant to delay or obstruct the investigation, which reflects his bona fide conduct.
10. Further continued incarceration would serve no useful purpose, especially when the trial is not likely to conclude in the near future.

A prolonged pre-trial detention becomes punitive even before conviction, and violates the fundamental rule i.e. bail is the rule and jail the exception, particularly when the accused does not pose a flight risk or a threat to the integrity of the trial.

11. There is also no likelihood of the applicant absconding, given that he is a well-settled individual,
has deep roots in society, and is the primary caregiver for his aged and ailing parents, who are dependent on him for their well-being as well as for his 8 year old son who has a medical history of cardio.

12. In any case, I am of the view that, otherwise, it is a case of bail given that the petitioner has already undergone incarceration of 2 years 2 months, at this stage duration of custody also makes out a case of bail.

13. Accordingly, the application is allowed and applicant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing of bail bond and surety to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Judge/Duty Judge as the case may be and subject to the This is a digitally signed order.
